label: fused-encode-blake3-column-hash
note: Fused RS-encode -> Blake3 column-hash streaming commitment (commit_stream.py): the 20.4 GB codeword never leaves L2 (512-1024-row slices, CUDA graph); B shape 310,602 rows: 46.7 ms/batch = 0.150 us/row = 11.4 us/VU, 436 GB/s of codeword, peak device memory 6.3 GiB (was 20.6). vs unfused encode 32.2 + Blake3 56.6 = 88.8 ms: 1.90x; vs encode + SHA-256 78 ms: 1.67x. Halves: encoder in L2 slices 35.7 ms (compute-bound: the SIMT NTT is now the bottleneck), Blake3 chunk kernel with the message schedule unrolled 15.4 ms (1.32 TB/s; hash_gpu's Blake3 was 359 GB/s: the reference-style m[MSG_PERM[i]] loop spilled). Bit-exact vs the unfused path (v2 + hash_gpu.merkle) and vs blake3/hashlib on CPU. A shape 7.4 ms (1.96x). keep_codeword (cosets streamed to a 15.3 GB store for the tests/openings): +2.3 ms.

label: fused-encode-sha256-column-hash
note: Same pipeline with SHA-256 sequential column states (protocol leaf H(column)): B 58.3 ms/batch = 0.188 us/row = 14.2 us/VU, 1.34x vs unfused 78 ms; SHA-256 half 30.0 ms alone = 678 GB/s, at the 4090's INT32 issue rate (~2,000 int ops per 64 B block): SHA-256 cannot go faster on this card; 16,384 sequential chains = 4 warps/SM. A shape 9.3 ms. Two-stream overlap of encoder and hash gives nothing: both are ALU-bound SIMT kernels (the encoder at 64-120 registers x 512-1024 threads owns every register of the SM).

note: B-Ligero linear test on the 8,192-point domain: per witness row encode the 6 BabyBear coordinate rows of r^T A on coset 1 and the witness row on coset 1 (7 v2 encoder calls, ncosets=1), product-accumulate over 310,602 rows (combine_linear, 256-row L2 slices, CUDA graph): 149.4 ms per B batch = 0.48 us/row = 36.5 us/VU. label: ligero-quadratic-test+irs+inversions+openings
note: B's small buckets on the 4090 (bit-exact vs numpy / Python-int F_c): quadratic test p_0 (33,485 product rows, x/y/z re-encoded on coset 1, combine_quadratic) 7.8 ms; IRS row combination v = r^T W over the k-wide rows (F_c scalar per row, 5.09 GB read once) 5.7 ms = 0.89 of the HBM read floor, 1.35 T mont-mul/s; helper batch inversion of 125.9M BabyBear^6 elements (Montgomery trick, strided ownership, Fermat inversion per 481-element segment) 28.8 ms = 0.23 ns/element, 0.52 of its 15 ms traffic floor; 192 column openings: gather from the kept cosets store 3.75 ms (+1.3 ms host Merkle paths) or re-encode with the gather-mode encoder 32.2 ms. Sum 47 ms = 11.5 us/VU.
